mark_breakdown.desc: Apply reverse chain rule $\int (ax+b)^n dx = \frac{(ax+b)^{n+1}}{a(n+1)} + c$

step_by_step: Identify linear inner function $u = 3x - 5$ with $a = 3$ and exponent $n = 3$.
Increase power by 1 to 4 and divide by $4 \times 3$.
Combine the constants to obtain $\frac{1}{12}(3x-5)^4 + c$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting to divide by the inner derivative $a = 3$.

mark_breakdown.desc: Rewrite with negative fractional index and apply reverse chain rule
Correct coefficient and simplified radical form

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Express the square root in the denominator as a negative fractional power $(4-x)^{-1/2}$ and use linear substitution.
step_by_step: Multiply by the outer constant $2$ to get $-4\sqrt{4-x} + c$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting the factor of $-1$ from the derivative of $(4-x)$.
